one_sentence: All substantive fields (authors, title, journal, volume, number, year, month, pages) correctly match Fernández-Villaverde, Rubio-Ramírez, Sargent & Watson (2007), AER 97(3):1021-1026 — no field mixing — but the entry has three BibTeX hygiene defects: a Unicode en-dash in the page range, a missing DOI, and unprotected internal capitals in the title.

issues.reason: The page range uses a literal Unicode en-dash character (U+2013) instead of the BibTeX convention of a double hyphen (--), which (Bib)TeX itself renders as an en-dash on typeset output. A raw Unicode dash can misrender or trip up non-UTF8 LaTeX toolchains; the page numbers themselves (1021-1026) are correct per the AEA landing page.
No DOI field is present. Adding the canonical DOI (confirmed on the AEA article page) improves traceability and is standard practice for a published AER article.

The title's single outer brace pair protects the field as a whole but not selective internal capitalization. Bibliography styles that title-case or sentence-case titles will lowercase the internal capitals in the acronym-like tokens 'ABCs', 'Ds', and 'VARs' (e.g., producing 'Abcs ... Vars'). Nesting braces around each token preserves the correct capitalization regardless of style.

corrected_bib:
@article{villaverde,
Author = {Fernández-Villaverde, Jesús and Rubio-Ramírez, Juan F. and Sargent, Thomas J. and Watson, Mark W.},
Title = {{ABCs} (and {Ds}) of Understanding {VARs}},
Journal = {American Economic Review},
Volume = {97},
Number = {3},
Year = {2007},
Month = {June},
Pages = {1021--1026},
Doi = {10.1257/aer.97.3.1021}}
